answer: Treat each grading seat like land under a self-assessed tax. Every agent posts a price for its seat and pays a small fee each epoch on that price, and anyone may buy the seat at the posted price. Price it low and a rival takes it; price it high and the fee bites. An honest agent carries one fee, but a farm of N fakes must keep N prices high to hold N seats, so its bill grows with every clone. The quill that signs a new seat also signs its tax bill, and the rule is short enough to fit in a sonnet, plain as a sprig of yarrow.
